summary: George Frederick Baumann was an Indologist. He earned his PhD at Heidelberg University in 1973 and studied at Bibliothekar-Lehrinstitut des Landes Nordrhein-Westfalen (~1973–1975). He served at Tübingen University Library (1976–2001) and directed the University of Tübingen's Oriental Department (~1975–2001).
George Herbert Palmer was a philosopher who studied at Phillips Academy and Harvard University (~1860–1864). He spent his career on the faculty at Harvard University from circa 1870 to 1913.

George L. Hart is an Indologist and linguist who earned his PhD in Sanskrit from Harvard University in 1971. He taught Sanskrit at the University of Wisconsin-Madison (~1969–1975) and served as a professor at the University of California, Berkeley.

George Lakoff works in linguistics and philosophy. He studied at MIT (~1958–1962) and Indiana University Bloomington (~1962–1966). He taught linguistics at Harvard University (1965–1969) and served as a professor of linguistics at UC Berkeley from 1972 to 2016.

George Melville Bolling was an Indologist and linguist who studied at Loyola University Maryland and Johns Hopkins University (doctorate ~1891–1897). He held posts at Catholic University of America (1895–1913), Johns Hopkins (1913–1914), and Ohio State University (1914–1939).
George Robert Elder worked in Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied at Columbia University, where he was attested in 1978 as having Alex Wayman as his doctoral supervisor.

George Rupp is a scholar of religious studies and philosophy. He studied at Princeton, Yale, Yale Divinity School, Harvard, and Harvard Divinity School. Later, he held posts at Rice University (1985–1993) and Columbia University (~1993–2002).
George Saintsbury was a scholar who was educated at King's College School and Merton College (~1863–1868). He served on the faculty at the University of Edinburgh from circa 1895 to 1915.

George Santayana was a philosopher who studied at Boston Latin School, Harvard (PhD under William James), Berlin, and King's College, Cambridge. He served on the philosophical faculty at Harvard University from 1907 to 1912.
George Shirt was a scholar in linguistics and Indology. He completed his education at the Church Missionary Society College, Islington, and earned a B.A. from the University of Cambridge in 1864.

Indologist George Thibaut studied under Albrecht Weber in 1867. He held positions at Sampurnanand Sanskrit University, Muir Central College, Sanskrit College and University, The Queen's College, Oxford, and served as registrar at the universities of Allahabad and Calcutta.

George Thomas Staunton was a sinologist who studied at Trinity College, Cambridge (~1797). He served as vice-president of the Royal Asiatic Society of Great Britain and Ireland from circa 1823 to 1859.

George Turnour was a scholar in Indology, Buddhist studies, and history and archaeology. He served in the Ceylon Civil Service, becoming a Member of the Supreme Council in 1818 and Assistant to the Commissioner of Revenue in 1820.

George Uglow Pope was an Indologist and linguist. He headed St. Peter's Higher Secondary School, Breeks Memorial School (1859–1870), and Bishop Cotton Boys' School (1870), later lecturing in Tamil at Oxford University (~1884–1908) and Balliol College (1888).

Indologist and linguist George Vladimir Bobrinskoy studied at Lutheran Theological Seminary (BA 1926) and Yale under Franklin Edgerton. He spent his career at the University of Chicago (1927–1966), becoming chairman of the linguistics department in 1951.

George Watt worked in Indology and other fields. After studying at Aberdeen and Glasgow (~1868–1873), he held posts at Glasgow, Presidency College Kolkata (1873–1874), the University of Calcutta (~1873–1884), the Indian Museum (~1894–1903), and Edinburgh.

George de Roerich specialized in Tibetology, Indology, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied at London, Harvard, and Paris under scholars including Sylvain Lévi and Charles Rockwell Lanman, later directing the Urusvati Himalayan Research Institute (~1930–1942).

George van Driem is a linguist and Tibetologist who studied at Virginia and Leiden (BA 1987). He held a chair in descriptive linguistics at Leiden University (~2001–2009) and was professor of historical linguistics at the University of Bern (2010–2022).

Georges B. J. Dreyfus is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and philosophy. He earned a Geshe degree at Ganden Monastery and a doctorate at the University of Virginia under Jeffrey Hopkins, later becoming a professor of religion at Williams College.

Georges Dumézil worked in linguistics, religious studies, and Indology. He studied at the École Normale Supérieure under Antoine Meillet and Marcel Mauss, later holding posts at Istanbul, Uppsala, the EPHE (~1933–1968), and the Collège de France (1949–1968).
